country.comment: Empirical dataset covers Brazilian municipalities and subnational sanitation regulatory agencies recognized by ANA.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumo Estruturado; PDF p. 2, Structured Abstract; PDF p. 10, Section 4

effect_estimate.comment: Note a typo in Table 3 stub where the second row is labeled 'eleicoes_municipais' instead of 'eleicoes_estaduais', clarified in the accompanying text on PDF p. 13. Network expansion reductions from political interference are derived theoretically (Propositions 1-2 and Corollaries 1-2), while real tariff variation is the empirical dependent variable and water/sewage coverage rates are covariates.
effect_estimate.value: Municipal election years are negatively associated with real regulated water/sanitation tariff variation across all panel specifications (Fixed Effects: -0.243, SE = 0.120, p < 0.05; Pooled OLS: -0.281, SE = 0.119, p < 0.05; Random Effects: -0.278, SE = 0.118, p < 0.05; N = 983), with mean real tariff adjustments of -0.0049 in municipal election years (n = 302) vs. 0.0075 in state election years (n = 227) and 0.0081 in non-election years (n = 613). State election years are negative and marginally significant only in Fixed Effects (-0.185, SE = 0.110, p < 0.10). Water coverage rate is negatively associated with real tariff variation (Fixed Effects: -2.101, SE = 1.082, p < 0.10; Pooled OLS: -2.078, SE = 0.0498, p < 0.01; Random Effects: -2.112, SE = 0.518, p < 0.01), while sewage coverage is non-significant (Fixed Effects: 0.136, SE = 0.611). Theoretically, electoral interference lowers regulated price markups below the Ramsey benchmark and reduces optimal second-period network expansion.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 9-10, Section 3.2 (Proposição 2, Corolário 2); PDF p. 12, Table 2; PDF p. 13, Section 4.1 and Table 3

mechanism_certainty.comment: Statistical association documented in municipality-year panel regressions between election-year cycles, water coverage rates and real regulated tariff adjustments; political interference inside regulatory agencies is proxied by election-year indicators rather than directly observed, and downstream effects on network investment/expansion are modeled theoretically rather than estimated as an empirical outcome.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 9-10, Section 3.2; PDF pp. 11-14, Sections 4.1-4.2 and Table 3

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines political/electoral interference by municipal and state politicians over subnational regulatory agencies (political_coordination), discretionary tariff regulation and ordinary contract revisions (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, discretion), and regulated water/sanitation tariff pricing/markups (BURDEN, fees).
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 5, Section 2; PDF pp. 6-10, Section 3; PDF pp. 10-14, Section 4

outcome_flags.comment: Theoretical model analyzes water/sanitation network expansion via new connections and universal service coverage (n_2, n_t/N) as well as per-user water consumption quantity (q); empirical regressions use municipal water supply coverage (atend_agua, SNIS AG001) and sanitary sewerage coverage (atend_esgoto, SNIS ES001) alongside real regulated tariff adjustments (Variacao_real).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 5-10, Section 3; PDF pp. 10-13, Section 4, Table 1 and Table 3

publication_year.comment: Published December 21, 2023 in Revista de Defesa da Concorrencia v. 11, n. 2.
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header and footnote 1

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Empirical component is an observational longitudinal municipality-year panel study (2002-2021) examining recurring electoral cycles and coverage covariates without evaluating a discrete policy intervention; note substantial selection bias acknowledged by authors (excluding municipalities with zero tariff adjustments over the entire period and imputing 0% when regulators did not respond).
risk_of_bias_tool.value: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

sample_size.comment: Unbalanced panel from 2002 to 2021; exact number of unique municipalities/providers in the final panel is not reported, though Table 1 reports N = 1,142 for tariff adjustments/population, N = 1,118 for water coverage, and N = 983 for sewage coverage (which determines N = 983 in Table 3 regressions).
sample_size.value: 1,142 municipality-year observations (2002-2021) in descriptive statistics; 983 municipality-year observations in panel regression models (sourced from 88 ANA-recognized subnational sanitation regulatory agencies: 46 municipal, 26 state and 16 intermunicipal)

study_design.comment: Combines a formal microeconomic regulatory model (two periods with an interim election) with an empirical unbalanced panel data regression analysis comparing Pooled OLS, Fixed Effects (selected via Hausman test) and Random Effects specifications.
study_design.value: Two-period dynamic regulatory theoretical model combined with an observational longitudinal municipality-year panel econometric study (pooled OLS, municipality fixed effects and random effects regressions, 2002-2021)
